title: Error Forensics Panel — request failure taxonomy & payload inspector
creator: Maya R. Chen
description:
Goal: Design an "error forensics" panel in Redwood Console that helps engineers quickly triage failed requests, understand retry behavior, and inspect relevant payloads while preserving user privacy and staying within storage cost targets. The panel will be available from per-route and per-model dashboards and from the global incident timeline.

Scope:
- Top-level summary: error rate, retries, most-common error categories (taxonomy), and recent sample failures.
- Request timeline: chronological list with filter and search (by request_id, model, tenant, date range).
- Error taxonomy filters: client (4xx), server (5xx), inference (model output/decoding), quota/rate-limit, network/timeout, runtime (out-of-gpu memory), signature/validation.
- Payload Inspector: expandable side panel that shows request metadata, redacted request/response bodies, key fields (prompt length, token count, kv_cache_hit/miss), and links to raw logs/trace. Support for switching sampling redaction level (none, redact PII, show metadata-only) via a policy toggle.
- Retry visualization: show retry chains (original request -> retry attempts), outcomes, and suggested root causes (e.g., transient infra issue vs. invalid payload).
- Quick actions: re-run request (with caution), open support ticket, copy diagnostic bundle (sanitized).

Telemetry & backend contract (needs ENG): required fields per sampled failure: request_id, timestamp, route, model, tenant_id (hashed), error_code, error_message_category, latency_ms, token_count, retry_count, kv_cache_hit, backend_region, infra_error_code (if any). Optional: full request/response payload stored in configurable retention with encryption.

Privacy & cost trade-offs: storing full payloads rapidly increases S3/DB costs and raises PII risk. Proposal: default to metadata-only sampling at 7d retention; allow opt-in hashed payload capture for enterprise with KMS and longer retention. All payload views must redact or mask common PII by default (emails, credit-card-ish patterns) and surface a clear banner explaining data retention policy.

Acceptance criteria:
- Figma prototype of the panel and inspector with desktop and tablet layouts (links in comments).
- Usability test with 3 platform engineers: complete triage scenario in <6 minutes.
- Design spec for redaction levels and copy for privacy banner.
- Implementation handoff doc listing telemetry fields and API endpoints (sample payloads).
